newsitem.title: USA: Bill introduced to curb U.S. federal court powers.
newsitem.headline: Bill introduced to curb U.S. federal court powers.

text.p: A bill to limit the power of federal courts over state referendums was introduced Wednesday by the chairman and several Republican members of the House Judiciary Committee.

The bill would require a three-judge federal panel to rule on constitutional challenges to referendums passed by voters in a state and would prohibit a federal court from imposing a tax to enforce a law or decision.

"This bill recognises that state referenda reflect, more than any other process, the one-person/one-vote system and seeks to protect a fundamental part of our national foundation," Judiciary Committee Chairman Henry Hyde, Republican of Illinois, said in a statement.

The bill was in response to the action of a federal judge who issued an injunction barring enforcement of a proposition passed by California voters last year to prohibit government-sponsored race and gender preferences in hiring. A three-judge federal panel in California Tuesday lifted the injunction and upheld the constitutionality of Proposition 209.
The ban on court-imposed taxes was in response to cases in which a judge has required a state or local government to raise taxes to enforce a judgment.
Hyde and other sponsors said only legislatures, not judges, should have the power to raise taxes. Hyde said the bill was needed to restore the balance of power between the branches of government.

Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Orrin Hatch, R-Utah, said he was planning to introduce similar legislation in the Senate. "I believe that Congress has an obligation to exercise its authority, within proper bounds, to do what it can to limit judicial abuses that undermine our democratic system," Hatch said in a statement.
